name: AlohaMini
description: A bimanual teleoperation and imitation-learning research rig, not a navigation robot — the mobile base and lift exist to position two arms for pick-and-place manipulation, controlled by physically puppeteering a matching leader arm. Built by independent makers on Hugging Face's LeRobot ecosystem (SO-ARM100 arms, a LeKiwi-derived base), not by Stanford/Berkeley's original ALOHA team or Trossen Robotics, despite the shared name.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: Pro/Edu tier, per AlohaMini's official site; DIY kit is ~13.5kg

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: no official L×W×H figure found in this research

specs.label: Compute
specs.note: swappable for Jetson Orin Nano or any USB3 SBC

specs.label: Software
specs.note: ACT, Diffusion Policy, Pi-0.5, SmolVLA — data collection, not a pre-trained robot

specs.label: Arms
specs.note: AM-ARM200, 6+1 DOF each; Feetech STS3215/STS3095 bus servos

specs.label: Mobile Base
specs.note: up to 70kg load rating (current AlohaMini2 generation)

specs.label: Control
specs.note: a human puppeteers a matching arm — not joystick-driven

sourcing: Specs compiled from the AlohaMini GitHub repository, its published bill of materials, and the project's own site as of this build. Manufacturer legal-entity claims and pricing outside the project's own BOM were not independently verifiable — confirm before purchase.

pricing.summary: Pricing is scattered across sources: a DIY self-build from the project's own published bill of materials runs roughly $950–$1,100 in parts, and the project's own site lists assembled "Pro" tiers from $1,499 up to $2,699 for the 6-DOF version. A pre-built unit sold through third-party reseller PartaBot at $1,099 is currently out of stock/preorder-only, so that cheaper path isn't presently available.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: AlohaMini is an independent open-source project — not built by Stanford/Berkeley's ALOHA research team or Trossen Robotics — assembled from Hugging Face LeRobot community hardware (TheRobotStudio's SO-ARM100 arm design and a LeKiwi-derived base), with real CAD, bill of materials, and code published under Apache-2.0. A separate claim of TechCrunch coverage and Hugging Face leadership endorsement, seen on one reseller's page, could not be verified anywhere else and isn't repeated here.
